svg.title: How the ROCKE-3D JAX hybrid baseline relates to Fortran
svg.desc: Diagram showing a full Fortran reference run supplying restart and recorded comparison data, a JAX GPU run computing its accelerated stages and calling the original Fortran radiation server, with measured timing and explicit limits on performance claims.
svg.text: How to read the JAX–Fortran baseline
A hybrid performance test can reuse Fortran as an oracle and as the live radiation component—without porting or rerunning the whole Fortran model every time.
Key idea
Run the full Fortran model to create the reference once; run JAX for the work being tested; call original Fortran only for the accepted radiation boundary.
1 Reference / oracle: full Fortran, run separately

Only RADIA runs in Fortran at runtime—not

svg.text: Replay mode — useful control, not full-work performance

text.tspan: • Radiation outputs are read from saved Fortran records; RADIA is not run.
• Holds radiation fixed, so developers can isolate and profile the JAX stages.
• It skips radiation computation: do not compare its runtime to full Fortran
as if both performed the same amount of work.

svg.text: Replay answers: “How fast are these stages with radiation held fixed?”
Live-server mode — real radiation, still a hybrid

text.tspan: • On scheduled radiation steps, the original Fortran RADIA/SOCRATES is called;
between them, the returned heating is held as in the model cadence.
• This avoids porting radiation and counts its actual cost in the JAX run.
• It is a valid test of this hybrid design—but recorded inputs elsewhere mean
it is not yet proof that every physics stage was computed in both runs.

svg.text: Live radiation ≠ full Fortran model; it is one Fortran component inside JAX.
3 What the current baseline says—and the boundary of the claim
Measured hybrid result (V100)

text.tspan: 16-step live-radiation cycle: 3.40–3.57 s/step
Optional template prefetch: 3.33 s/step
Owner marked 3.5 s challenge MET (speed only).

svg.text: Known limits of this result

text.tspan: Day-1; some land / Ent / template / packet
inputs are recorded; it is hybrid, not all-JAX.
Strict day-fidelity criterion remains NOT MET.

svg.text: What is still needed for “faster than Fortran”

text.tspan: Equivalent computed work; same restart/window;
matched target hardware / cores; include compile
and callback costs; report fidelity separately.

svg.text: Bottom line: reuse the full Fortran run as a reference; invoke only original Fortran radiation at runtime. This avoids porting and rerunning all Fortran for every JAX iteration.
Evidence: Reports/GPU_V100_VS_A100.md; Reports/PERFORMANCE_BUDGET_3P5S.md; Reports/ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md (checked 2026-10-11).
